the activities of HIF1-alpha, AP-1, and NF-kappaB were increased in hypoxic liver, while the expression of VEGFA, ET1, iN0s and eNOS were increased in the hypoxic livers.
the hepatic response in the chronic hypoxia model was associated with increased activity of Hif-1α, Ap-1 and Nf-kb.
chronic hypoxia induces the activation of HIF-α, AP- 1 and NF- κB, which in turn increases the expression of iNOS and VEGF in the liver.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms underlying the hepatic response in the rat model of chronic hypoxia.
the molecular mechanisms of chronic hypoxia-induced liver damage.
the role of HIF-α, AP- 1 and NF- κB in hepatic response to hypoxia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic hypoxia may cause liver cell injury through the activation of HIF-α1, NF-κβ and AP-1.
the hepatic response under chronic hypoxemia is characterized by the increased activities of nuclear transcriptional factors (HIF-α, NF- κB and AP- 1) and increased expression of downstream genes.
hypoxia is not a major factor in causing liver injury, but may play an important role in liver adaptation to chronic hypoxemia.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic hypoxia can activate the expression and activities of HIF1α, AP1, NF-kB, iNOS, e-NOS, ET- 1 and VEGFA.
the hypoxic liver is a complex organ with a variety of responses to hypoxia.
hypoxia may cause liver cell injury through the increased activity of Hif-1 alpha, AP-1, and NF-kappaB, which may lead to increased expression of iNOS and VEGF, as well as ET-1, and eNOS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
hypoxia can induce liver injury, and this injury may be due to increased oxidative stress.
hypoxia may be involved in the development of chronic liver disease.
chronic hypoxia may cause liver injury through increased expression of inflammatory and angiogenic genes.
